## How it works

- [statement] The cited bot setup guide says Amount per trade applies separately to each selected pair and warns that simultaneous deals can cause insufficient balance. Its Summary-box documentation says bots and pairs compete for the same available funds, so their full requirements must be added. (medium confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16281102-how-the-dca-bot-works-strategy-setup-guide · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion · also: https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16666593-understanding-the-dca-bot-summary-box
- [statement] Bitsgap says a price-step DCA ladder struggles when price grinds downward without a meaningful bounce, because every safety order can fill and the ladder runs out. Block Research describes the same path as locking capital in unrealized drawdown after the last safety order. (medium confidence) — https://bitsgap.com/blog/what-is-a-dca-bot-the-averaging-ladder-explained · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion · also: https://blockresearch.ai/blog/dca-bot
- [statement] The term Amount per trade has different meanings in the cited vendor guides: the cited bot setup guide defines it as the initial position size, while Cornix defines Amount Per Trade as the total potential amount assigned to a complete DCA cycle. (medium confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16281102-how-the-dca-bot-works-strategy-setup-guide · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion · also: https://cornix.io/dca-bot-settings/
- [statement] Cornix states that Stop Loss Timeout can delay closure after the stop price is reached. It separately documents a continuous-stop count to deactivate the bot, a cooldown after trade close, and a total-cycle count before manual reactivation. (low confidence) — https://cornix.io/dca-bot-settings/ · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion
- [statement] OKX distinguishes nominal leverage from effective leverage: increasing position value without increasing margin raises effective leverage even if the nominal setting stays fixed. Its estimated-liquidation calculation assumes orders fill sequentially and stops if the liquidation price rises above the next execution price, so that estimate does not assume the bot can always reach every remaining safety order. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/whats-futures-dca-bot-and-how-do-i-maximize-my-efficiency-with-automated · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] After price falls beyond the deepest safety order, the cited Summary-box documentation says the bot has spent its safety orders, holds the position, and cannot improve the average with further safety orders. (low confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16666593-understanding-the-dca-bot-summary-box · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion
- [statement] OKX states that a futures DCA position may be liquidated if its margin balance falls below maintenance margin and that this can lose the initial funds. Bitsgap also distinguishes futures DCA liquidation risk from its spot DCA description. (medium confidence) — https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/whats-futures-dca-bot-and-how-do-i-maximize-my-efficiency-with-automated · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion · also: https://bitsgap.com/blog/what-is-a-dca-bot-the-averaging-ladder-explained
- [statement] The cited the cited bot setup guide setup guide says Max Open Positions limits the cumulative number of open strategies across DCA bots and ignores or cancels new trade signals until an existing strategy closes when that limit is reached. (low confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16281102-how-the-dca-bot-works-strategy-setup-guide · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The cited bot setup guide allows take-profit to use either the initial order or the average position price. A basket target tied to average entry is therefore a configuration choice in that guide, rather than a universal property of every DCA bot. (low confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16281102-how-the-dca-bot-works-strategy-setup-guide · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion
- [statement] The cited Summary-box documentation defines maximum price drop covered as the deviation of the final safety order. Its cumulative-step formula is deviation(k) = p x (c^k - 1) / (c - 1) when c differs from 1, and p x k when c equals 1. (low confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16666593-understanding-the-dca-bot-summary-box · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion
- [statement] The cited Summary-box documentation defines required capital as the base order plus every safety order. For a safety-order volume multiplier m that differs from 1, it gives Required = V0 + V1 x (m^n - 1) / (m - 1). (low confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16666593-understanding-the-dca-bot-summary-box · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion
- [statement] Bitsgap warns that weak liquidity and wide spreads can consume the small take-profit targets used by its DCA bot. This is a vendor description of execution risk, rather than independent evidence of a profitable coin-selection threshold. (low confidence) — https://bitsgap.com/blog/what-is-a-dca-bot-the-averaging-ladder-explained · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion
- [statement] Bitsgap describes averaging down as lowering average entry while adding exposure during a continued decline, and says it does not protect against a market that keeps falling. Block Research explicitly calls buying more as price drops a mechanic rather than an edge. These are scoped descriptions and commentary, rather than a measured positive expected-return result for the ladder itself. (medium confidence) — https://bitsgap.com/blog/what-is-a-dca-bot-the-averaging-ladder-explained · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion · also: https://blockresearch.ai/blog/dca-bot

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Bitsgap describes its price-step DCA bot as a base order followed by lower safety orders and a whole-position take-profit above the average entry. Block Research distinguishes this price-triggered averaging-down from time-based DCA at a fixed interval. (medium confidence) — https://bitsgap.com/blog/what-is-a-dca-bot-the-averaging-ladder-explained · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion · also: https://blockresearch.ai/blog/dca-bot
- [statement] The cited Summary-box documentation recommends leaving available-balance headroom for fees, slippage and other bots. It states that its summary figures assume all safety orders fill and exclude fees and slippage. (low confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16666593-understanding-the-dca-bot-summary-box · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion
- [statement] Bitsgap describes pullbacks followed by partial recoveries as the favorable path for its DCA bot. It says a straight upward move after the base order leaves only that small initial buy in the trade. (low confidence) — https://bitsgap.com/blog/what-is-a-dca-bot-the-averaging-ladder-explained · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion
- [statement] OKX warns that a martingale strategy can increase spending rapidly after a few transactions, especially during a prolonged price decline, and that exiting after funds run out can produce high losses. (low confidence) — https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/whats-futures-dca-bot-and-how-do-i-maximize-my-efficiency-with-automated · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion
- [statement] Both the cited the cited bot setup guide setup guide and the Cornix settings guide allow a stop-loss baseline to use either the initial/first entry or the average entry. (medium confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16281102-how-the-dca-bot-works-strategy-setup-guide · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion · also: https://cornix.io/dca-bot-settings/
- [statement] Bitsgap qualifies its platform profit-rate analysis as pooling real-money and demo bots and removing unfinished launches, small deposits and outliers; it also says the typical size of losses is not published. Separately, Block Research describes frequent small closed wins alongside a large unrealized open loss. These source-specific disclosures show why a closed-profit rate alone does not quantify whole-account losses or expected returns. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://bitsgap.com/blog/what-is-a-dca-bot-the-averaging-ladder-explained · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion · also: https://blockresearch.ai/blog/dca-bot
- [statement] The cited the cited bot setup guide setup guide distinguishes Position averaging, which begins applying its order-size multiplier from the second extra order, from Order averaging, which applies it from the first extra order. It also distinguishes fixed coin amount from fixed quote-currency order value. A ladder capital calculation must identify which of these documented configurations it represents. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16281102-how-the-dca-bot-works-strategy-setup-guide · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion
- [statement] OKX documents a configuration-specific exception to an assumed positive liquidation price: for a long Futures DCA position, an absent estimated liquidation price may mean its margin is sufficient that it would not liquidate even at a zero asset price. The documentation uses "may"; absence of the displayed price alone is not an unconditional safety guarantee. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/whats-futures-dca-bot-and-how-do-i-maximize-my-efficiency-with-automated · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion
- [statement] Stopping new activity need not release an existing position: the cited bot setup guide documents a Stop choice that leaves trades open and monitored, while OKX says pausing its Futures DCA bot cancels pending orders but retains the current position and keeps TP/SL active. These documented controls therefore require an explicit distinction between pausing new orders and closing inventory. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16281102-how-the-dca-bot-works-strategy-setup-guide · keywords: Averaging-down DCA bots and capital exhaustion · also: https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/whats-futures-dca-bot-and-how-do-i-maximize-my-efficiency-with-automated
